assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration correction opened the door to routine sub-angstrom imaging and spectroscopy of atoms in materials. It is a genuine invention, experimentally demonstrated, that has transformed materials physics, interfaces, catalysis and 2D materials. The electron microscope itself was recognised in 1986, but this later step removed the resolution limit set by lens aberrations.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the corrector theory and optical design; Haider built and demonstrated the working hexapole corrector for the TEM together with Rose and Urban; Urban led the first application to atomic-resolution materials imaging. Work on the STEM corrector by researchers not in the supplied names means a three-person split is defensible but not perfectly clean.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: about twenty-five years of independent confirmation, commercial instruments worldwide and stable results. Recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether STEM-corrector pioneers outside the credited names should share recognition under the original-experiment criterion.
I work in this field and must guard against favouritism; priority details are from memory and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The magic-angle flat-band prediction and the 2018 observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created a new field, moire quantum matter. It is an original, clear discovery with broad consequences for correlated electron physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 prediction of the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the original experimental discovery of the correlated and superconducting states. All three seem to have decisive roles. The students and postdocs on the 2018 papers cannot be credited under the prize rules.
assessment.maturity: Replicated by many groups within a few years, though the field is still moving. Timing is early but defensible.
uncertainties: Mechanism of the superconductivity is not settled.
Recognition may be judged premature relative to older candidates.
Weight to give the theoretical prediction versus the experiment is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock concept and its realisation delivered clocks with fractional uncertainty near 1e-18, a new level of measurement with relevance for the second, geodesy and tests of fundamental physics. It is a clear invention with experimental verification.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and first realised the lattice-clock concept; Ye brought the strontium clock to record accuracy and stability. Two laureates give a clean configuration, though others contributed early ideas and I cannot confirm every priority detail from memory.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by several independent laboratories with stable comparisons. Redefinition of the SI second has not yet happened, so the full impact is still prospective.
uncertainties: Possible competing claims for early lattice-clock concepts.
Impact on the SI second is still prospective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2008 discovery of superconductivity in doped LaFeAsO at about 26 K, followed by a rapid rise above 50 K, established a second major family of high-temperature superconductors and a new test bed for unconventional pairing. It is an original experimental discovery.
assessment.attribution: Hosono's group made the original discovery and is the clear primary credit. Xianhui Chen and Zhongxian Zhao reported important rapid increases in the transition temperature, but these were follow-on advances that do not meet the original-experiment criterion as clearly. A single laureate fits the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced everywhere within weeks and the materials class is firmly established. The pairing mechanism is still debated and applications are limited.
uncertainties: Practical benefit is limited so far.
Whether the committee wants to credit the follow-on transition-temperature advances.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube's observation of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos in 2013, and later source evidence, opened a new observational window on the universe. It is an instrument-driven discovery of high originality.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the project; Karle and Spiering held key construction and analysis roles. A collaboration of several hundred makes any three-person credit incomplete, and I cannot determine who made the decisive analysis steps. Earlier neutrino-telescope pioneers complicate priority.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is confirmed by further analyses, but source identification is still partial, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Collaboration-scale credit and the role of earlier pioneers.
Sources of most neutrinos remain unidentified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy centres at room temperature made solid-state spin qubits and nanoscale quantum sensors possible, with uses from biology to materials. It is a tool that lets us see what could not be seen before.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup's group made the original observation of single NV spins, and Jelezko and Wrachtrup developed their coherent control. Lukin's contributions to sensing and registers are important but later and more conceptual, so I propose the two original experimentalists.
assessment.maturity: Replicated in many laboratories, with commercial devices emerging. The basic science is mature while sensing applications continue to develop.
uncertainties: How much credit later sensing work by Lukin and others deserves.
Exact roles in the original demonstration are from memory and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite solar cells reached very high efficiency within about a decade, a remarkable materials development with direct societal relevance for energy.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitised cell, Park the more stable solid-state cell, and Snaith the thin-film planar devices. Credit is spread and the earliest contributors may not be fully captured by the supplied names, so attribution is more contested than for higher-ranked entries.
assessment.maturity: Efficiencies are widely reproduced, but long-term stability and toxicity are unresolved, so the technological outcome is not settled.
uncertainties: Distribution of credit among the early device reports.
Whether this is better recognised as chemistry or engineering rather than physics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators, together with the experimental observation of edge transport in HgTe quantum wells, founded a major area of condensed matter physics with both theory and experiment.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction; Molenkamp's group made the experimental realisation, following a HgTe-specific proposal by others who are not among the supplied names. A fair allocation is therefore difficult and the contributions need disentangling.
assessment.maturity: Many materials and experiments have confirmed the field, but device applications are limited. Recognition could be timely though contested.
uncertainties: Missing credit for the HgTe proposal by others.
Distinction between 2D and 3D topological insulators and their discoverers.
